purpose: Single source-of-truth research file containing all 55 genre contracts before any live Composer insertion.

current_profile_snapshot.scope_note: Project-controlled broad Rock baseline; not a universal definition of Rock.
current_profile_snapshot.groove_behavior: straight or lightly syncopated eighth-note rock pulse; backbeat remains structural but fills and pushes vary by section
current_profile_snapshot.phrase_behavior: 4- or 8-bar phrases with verse/chorus contrast, fills into boundaries, and selective lead call/response
current_profile_snapshot.harmony_behavior: tonal major/minor; power-chord, triadic, modal or blues-derived vocabulary; progression must vary across pieces
current_profile_snapshot.bass_behavior: electric bass locks with kick while retaining independent melodic movement; roots/fifths are a baseline, not a fixed template
current_profile_snapshot.percussion_behavior_if_applicable: kick/snare backbeat, hi-hat/ride timekeeping, tom/crash transitions; pattern variation required across sections
current_profile_snapshot.instrument_role_behavior: electric guitar rhythm + lead, electric bass, drum kit; optional acoustic guitar, keys, brass/strings via target resources
current_profile_snapshot.ensemble_player_behavior: rhythm section shares groove hierarchy; lead phrases leave space and answer vocal/melodic gaps
current_profile_snapshot.arrangement_transformation: verse/chorus or sectional builds; density, register and guitar texture change across sections
current_profile_snapshot.dynamic_behavior: firm but section-shaped; choruses may lift, breakdowns reduce density
current_profile_snapshot.articulation_behavior: guitar attacks, sustains, mutes, accents and slides follow role; drums use distinct backbeat/fill articulation
current_profile_snapshot.timing_humanization_behavior: shared groove offsets and phrase pushes; no independent random jitter
current_profile_snapshot.continuous_performance_control: velocity + expression + note length + target articulation controls
current_profile_snapshot.sound_effects_intent: amp/drive/reverb/delay are style resources, not mandatory; preserve bass clarity
current_profile_snapshot.mix_prominence_intent: kick/bass/rhythm foundation clear; lead present selectively rather than constantly
current_profile_snapshot.production_mastering_intent: punchy transients, controlled low-end, no automatic loudness flattening
current_profile_snapshot.manufacturer_adapter_requirements: map canonical guitars/bass/drums to target voices; do not replace genre because a patch is missing

current_profile_strengths: Good broad backbeat/guitar-bass-drums baseline.
Already requires section variation and lead space.

current_profile_gaps: Rock family is far too broad for one executable grammar.
No subgenre resolver or formation resolver.
No explicit rhythm-guitar versus lead-guitar agency model.

form_model.rule: Verse/chorus, through-composed, riff-based or progressive forms by subgenre; transitions and builds must be subgenre-specific.

harmony_model.rule: Power-chord, triadic, modal, blues-derived and extended vocabularies are selected by variant rather than mixed indiscriminately.

melody_model.rule: Vocal/lead/guitar melody occupies explicit foreground windows; hooks and riffs can carry structural identity.

rhythm_groove_model.rule: Backbeat/eighth/sixteenth feel, syncopation and subdivision are subgenre-specific; fills and pushes follow sections.

bass_model.rule: Bass locks with drums while retaining independent line shape, pickups and fills; root/fifth behavior is only one variant.

percussion_model.rule: Kick/snare/hats/ride/toms/crashes follow subgenre and section intensity; human timing/fill behavior can be derived from groove data.

phrase_model.rule: Riffs, vocal lines and lead fills share space; accompaniment does not answer every gap.

transition_model.rule: Drum fills, guitar texture shifts, stops, pickups and harmonic/riff changes are variant-specific.

development_model.rule: Develop through riff transformation, guitar texture, dynamics, register, harmony and section contrast.

cadence_ending_model.rule: Tags, stops, sustained hits, fades or composed endings by subgenre.

musical_agency_percent.rule: Agency is role-based and can rotate independently of amplified loudness or player count.

foreground_window_rules: Lead/vocal/guitar feature gets space through rhythm-guitar simplification, register and density.
Kick/bass remain foundation without owning every foreground moment.
A guitar solo window should alter the guitar's compositional role and thin competing harmonic layers before applying level changes.
Rock instrument-tag evidence strongly supports drums/bass/electric-guitar core as a candidate default for band variants, while synth/keys/acoustic/other colors remain subgenre-dependent.
role_handoff_rules: Foreground can move among vocal/lead guitar/keys/riff while rhythm section maintains identity.
Rhythm and lead guitar identities must remain explicit.

register_occupancy.rule: Separate bass/kick low-end, rhythm-guitar midrange and lead/vocal register enough to preserve clarity.

section_population_reference.note: Rock formations vary from power trios to multi-guitar/keyboard ensembles.

presence_research_reference_mtg_jamendo.interpretation: Research cross-check only. Tag absence does not mean an instrument is absent; uploader metadata is incomplete and multi-label.

gmd_drum_performance_reference.scope: 1,150 human drum performances, 13.6 hours, >22,000 measures; annotated by drummer-provided primary/secondary style, BPM, beat versus fill, time signature, duration and split.
interpretation_guardrails: Use GMD as human drum-performance evidence, not as a complete genre-definition source.
Tempo values in GMD are observed performance examples, not hard genre limits.
Beat and fill examples are separate labels; the Composer should distinguish sustained groove state from transition/fill state.
Do not infer bass, guitar, harmony or ensemble instrumentation from a drum-only corpus.
Do not convert human timing into independent random jitter; timing relationships must remain groove-coherent.
runtime_implications: Drum engine must have distinct groove/beat state and fill/transition state.
Rock fills should be selected/generated in relation to phrase and section boundaries, not pasted at fixed intervals.
Humanization should derive from coherent drummer timing/velocity behavior rather than per-hit random noise.

guitarset_role_reference.scope: 360 approximately 30-second acoustic-guitar excerpts: 6 players × comping/solo versions × 5 styles × 3 progressions × 2 tempi, with pitch/string/fret/chord/beat/downbeat/playing-style annotations.
interpretation_guardrails: The design is deliberately balanced, so track counts must not be interpreted as real-world instrument-presence percentages.
Use the paired comping/solo design to validate role-dependent guitar behavior, register, note density and articulation.
A guitar changing from accompaniment to foreground should change musical role, not merely gain.
Because GuitarSet is acoustic-guitar based, do not use its timbre as a universal Rock/Funk production target.
runtime_implications: Rhythm-guitar/comping and lead/solo guitar must be separate role states.
Foreground handoff to guitar requires changes in note density, register, phrasing and accompaniment behavior, not only volume.
When guitar becomes lead, other harmonic layers should simplify or change register as needed.

Use rankings to inform candidate instrumentation/variant priors, then resolve actual instrumentation from the selected genre variant.

foreground_window_rules: When a woodwind or other small section owns foreground material, accompaniment must create an audibility window through density, register, articulation and/or spatial separation rather than artificial loudness alone.
Large string population does not grant permanent foreground ownership.
Foreground transfer must be explicit and time-bounded; supporting sections retain musical agency without masking the current owner.

Corpus evidence supports frequent woodwind foreground ownership despite much smaller physical population; the arranger must create windows for flute, oboe, clarinet and bassoon rather than allowing string mass to mask them.
Foreground targets are variant- and composition-specific; observed corpus averages are validation references, not quotas.

Woodwind foreground does not imply string silence: corpus activity shows frequent simultaneous section activity. The arranger should thin or re-voice supporting mass rather than simply muting the orchestra.
When foreground changes, adjust accompaniment activity quality (density/register/articulation/voicing) before using level changes.

Because strings are normally active through much of the score, a woodwind foreground window does not require strings to disappear; it requires their role, register, density, articulation and spatial footprint to yield enough perceptual room.
When masking risk is detected, change accompaniment behavior before applying foreground gain.
role_handoff_rules: Theme/countertheme may transfer among strings, woodwinds, brass and solo desks when supported by the resolved variant.
During handoff, previous foreground material simplifies, sustains, changes register or yields rhythmic activity as needed for clarity.
Population mass remains stable while foreground authority changes dynamically.

register_occupancy.rule: Avoid chronic overlap of dense low strings/brass with featured middle/upper voices; register allocation follows role and variant.

spatial_footprint_percent.initial_rule: Section width/depth scales with ensemble type and seating tradition; not a loudness percentage.

activity_empirical_reference.source: Krause & Müller 2023, Hierarchical Classification for Instrument Activity Detection in Orchestral Music Recordings
activity_empirical_reference.dataset_scope: Approximately 14 hours of orchestral/opera recordings with aligned frame-level activity annotations.
activity_empirical_reference.definition: Activity delta_c = fraction of reference frames in which class c is active.
activity_empirical_reference.published_observation: Strings and woodwinds are the most common classes; many same-family instruments are jointly active for substantial portions of recordings.
guardrails: Do not invent exact activity percentages from prose or a figure.
Do not mix opera/vocal activity with instrumental-orchestra activity without subset filtering.
Use activity share separately from population mass and Hauptstimme foreground ownership.

presence_research_reference_mtg_jamendo.interpretation: Research cross-check only. Tag absence does not mean an instrument is absent; uploader metadata is incomplete and multi-label.

observed_foreground_time_reference_perce.methodology: Duration-weighted qstamp-to-next-annotation intervals across 70 instrumental orchestral annotation files. Excludes Bach B Minor Mass, Brahms Ein Deutsches Requiem, and Beethoven Symphony No.9 movement 4 because of choral foreground. Final trailing segment after each file's last annotation is not estimated because the annotation format defines segment endings by the next annotation.
interpretation_guardrails: These are observed Hauptstimme/main-melody shares in this corpus, not recommended gain values.
Do not use these percentages as physical population, presence, or total activity percentages.
Corpus repertoire is not balanced evenly across periods/composers; Beethoven is heavily represented.
Hauptstimme annotation intentionally chooses one primary melody instrument even when multiple instruments double the theme.
Use this evidence to support foreground-window and role-handoff logic, not to force every piece toward the corpus average.

population_vs_foreground_observation.key_finding: Physical population and foreground ownership are strongly different quantities. In the observed corpus, woodwinds carry a much larger share of annotated foreground than their physical population share, while strings retain the largest physical mass.
population_vs_foreground_observation.runtime_implication: Population controls ensemble mass; resolved foreground ownership controls audibility windows. Never derive one directly from the other.

activity_vs_foreground_observation.key_finding: High activity does not imply foreground ownership. Strings are active during about 91.7% of observed score time but carry about 50.9% of annotated Hauptstimme foreground; woodwinds are active during about 76.0% and carry about 41.6% of annotated foreground.
runtime_implication: The arranger may keep strings active under a woodwind lead, but must change string function when masking risk is high.

Preferred anti-masking actions are density reduction, sustain/longer note values, register separation, articulation softening, voicing redistribution, selective rests, and spatial separation before gain changes.
A featured flute/oboe/clarinet/bassoon should not require permanent loudness inflation to remain audible.

observed_activity_time_reference_percent.methodology: Duration-weighted qstamp intervals across the same 70 instrumental orchestral movements used for the foreground study. A family/type counts as active during an interval when at least one corresponding score part is sounding. Family values are temporal unions, not sums of member-instrument occupancies; families overlap in time.
interpretation_guardrails: These are occupancy/activity percentages, not population, gain, foreground ownership, or note-density percentages.
Family percentages overlap because multiple families can sound simultaneously.
An instrument type is counted active if at least one part of that type is sounding.
Corpus repertoire is not period-balanced and should not be used as a universal Classical target without variant splitting.
Use this reference to model when sections should thin, sustain, rest, or change register around the current foreground owner.
Family occupancy must be computed as a temporal union. Summing instrument occupancies within a family can double-count simultaneous parts.

correction_order: apply only limited level correction if still required
masking_risk_rules.success_condition: Foreground is clearly intelligible while the supporting ensemble retains believable mass and continuity.

cross_period_texture_role_reference.roles: Percentages below are shares of each sampled part's active annotated time.
findings: Flute role is frequently melodic or melody-combined in every sampled period/style; treating flute as merely decorative/background color is not supported.
Violin 1 can be strongly melodic, but its role mix changes substantially across repertoire and can include major harmonic/rhythmic support functions.
Horn 1 is predominantly harmonic/rhythmic support in these sampled movements, with smaller pure-melody shares.
Role distributions change enough across Mozart/Beethoven/Tchaikovsky/Dvorak to justify period/variant-specific Classical role probabilities rather than one universal profile.
guardrails: This is a four-movement representative validation sample, not a balanced corpus.
Do not convert these percentages directly into gain, population or runtime quotas.
Use them to validate section-role-state behavior and period/variant differentiation.
